note: Candidates reviewed for this update but not admitted, with the reason and the evidence that would reopen each.

entries.candidate: Tritax Manor Farm Data Centre, Slough: permitted status (Secretary of State appeal decision APP/J0350/W/25/3366043, 10 June 2026)
entries.reason: Planning permission for the data centre and BESS was granted on 10 June 2026 and Tritax reported on 27 July 2026 that the six-week challenge period ended without challenge, so the consent is in effect. Both dates are outside the 85-day window (on or after 29 July 2026), so this fragment admits the project as announced from the 5 August 2026 half-year report and records the consent as context, following the Telehouse West 2 precedent.
entries.reopen_condition: A dated in-window consent record for the development (for example a Slough Borough Council decision approving pre-commencement conditions on P/10076/013) would support permitted; a dated Tritax or contractor report of site preparation or construction at Manor Farm would refresh the project to an active stage.

entries.candidate: Civo first UK edge data centre, Hertfordshire (Civo Data Centre (Welwyn) Ltd, Tewin Road, Welwyn Garden City AL7 1BD; EA permit EPR/TP3723UA)
entries.reason: Civo's release of 22 September 2026 (local civo-first-of-40-edge-dcs-20260922.html, sha256 d5e98c9d5525...) announces the first of 40 UK edge data centres 'opening in Hertfordshire': it will open at 8 MW, rising to 38 MW on the same plot, and 'fit-out of the building is underway'. Civo's 7 October Behavox release repeats that the flagship edge site is in Hertfordshire. Neither names a town, address or plot. The Environment Agency installations register (ea-installations-civo.json, sha256 313860addaa2...) lists a new-medium-combustion-plant standard-rules permit EPR/TP3723UA registered on 23 September 2026 to 'Civo Data Centre (Welwyn) Ltd' at Tewin Road, Welwyn Garden City AL7 1BD, grid reference TL 24582 13168 (51.803284, -0.194568 with pyproj 3.7.1; 64 m from the AL7 1BD postcode centroid), and a Welwyn Hatfield weekly list (12 June 2026) shows a substation application 6/2026/0921/FULL at 17 Tewin Road. That makes Tewin Road the likely site, but the tie between the release's 'Hertfordshire site' and Tewin Road is inferred from the holder's name and timing: Civo's unveiling page carries a decorative '51.9022N' latitude near Stevenage, where third-party directories place an existing facility of Civo's integrated ServerChoice business, and the Welwyn Hatfield planning search and Companies House search are forms that were not used. The MCP registration alone is a generator permit, not development consent or a physical observation. No Atlas record lies within 2 km (nearest Google Waltham Cross, 17.2 km).
entries.reopen_condition: A Civo, Environment Agency, Welwyn Hatfield or contractor record that names the Tewin Road (or 17 Tewin Road) building as Civo's Hertfordshire edge data centre, dated within 90 days of the update, with fit-out, construction, completion or operation; then admit it with the EA permit grid reference as a site locator (or a planning red line).

entries.candidate: Stellanor Hemel Hempstead data centre (Hemel One, Boundary Way, HP2 7YU; acquired from Imagination Technologies; EA permit EPR/BP3621MH)
entries.reason: Not in the Atlas (no Stellanor, Imagination, Boundary Way or Hemel record; nearest Atlas site 25 km). The Environment Agency register (ea-installations-data.json, sha256 952f6eb8fd02...) lists a new-MCP standard-rules permit EPR/BP3621MH registered 13 August 2026 to Stellanor Datacenters Properties UK Limited at Boundary Way, Hemel Hempstead HP2 7YU, grid reference TL 08472 08428 (51.764036, -0.429593), a usable official locator. But the only operator statements found (April 2026 acquisition of the Imagination Technologies facility under a sale-and-service-back; May 2026 completion of the Redcentric portfolio) are outside the window and were seen only in syndicated copies; no dated in-window Stellanor statement of current operation was found, and a generator permit does not establish operation.
entries.reopen_condition: A dated (within 90 days) Stellanor or customer statement that the Hemel Hempstead facility operates, captured from a robots-permitted primary host; then admit it as operational with the EPR/BP3621MH grid reference as the site locator.

entries.candidate: Tritax Big Box Chelmsford data centre (Project Blackwater, BW1/BW2, Beaulieu Parkway, Beaulieu Park, Chelmsford, Essex; 125 MW of power)
entries.reason: Tritax's 5 August 2026 half-year report (source uk-south-p1-tritax-hy26-report) names its second scheme at Chelmsford: 125 MW of power with delivery scheduled for 2028, delivery expected in 2029 and formal marketing from July 2026, under a development management agreement entered in June 2026. That supports announced status, but no robots-permitted official locator was found: trade reports place a two-building campus on greenfield land bounded by Beaulieu Parkway and Loverose Way under an application by Tritax Chelmsford PropCo Limited, but publicaccess.chelmsford.gov.uk could not be reached and no reference, red line or grid reference was obtained. A road-bounded description is not a locator. Not in the Atlas.
entries.reopen_condition: A Chelmsford City Council record (application reference, site plan or grid reference) or another official locator for the Beaulieu Park plot, with a Tritax or council record dated within 90 days of the update.

entries.candidate: Telehouse West 2 (TW2), London Docklands: physical status understated by the announced record
entries.reason: Telehouse's own pages show TW2 has been under construction since before the record's 22 September 2026 announced observation: its news item dated 20 October 2025 (telehouse-tw2-breaks-ground.html, sha256 cf96d6776f53...) says Telehouse 'has today broken ground' on TW2 with Flynn as contractor, and the campus updates page (telehouse-campus-updates.html, sha256 7407969f5a04...; JSON-LD dateModified 31 July 2026) has a 'July 2026' entry reporting ground works and piling complete, the ground-floor slab complete and steelwork installation commenced. Both observations predate 22 September 2026, so they cannot refresh the record (refreshes must be strictly newer), and a status correction is outside this fragment's change types. Telehouse's news archive (re-checked 22 October 2026) has no item after 24 July 2026.
entries.reopen_condition: A dated Telehouse, contractor or council report of TW2 construction, completion or operation after 22 September 2026 (then refresh to that stage), or a reviewed status correction citing the 20 October 2025 groundbreaking and the July 2026 progress entry.

entries.candidate: Iron Mountain Data Centres LON-1, 724-729 Dundee Road, Slough SL1 4JU (EA bespoke permit application EPR/LP3020MX/A001)
entries.reason: The Environment Agency advertised Iron Mountain (UK) Data Centre Limited's new bespoke permit application EPR/LP3020MX/A001 on GOV.UK on 13 August 2026 (govuk-iron-mountain-sl14ju-advert-body.json, sha256 639ec5f6912e...; consultation 13 August to 11 September 2026, ea-consult-iron-mountain-sl14ju.html, sha256 29abdca06285...). The operator's non-technical summary (im-sl14ju-nts.pdf, sha256 bcc63344b6ac...; revision 2 dated 30 June 2026) describes 'Iron Mountain Data Centre LON-1' at 724-729 Dundee Road in the present tense: mains electricity supplies its operation, 11 standby generators installed between before 2018 and March 2021 (70.3 MWth) are maintained and tested, and its data-storage services are run under ISO 27001 and ISO 9001. Form Part B2 (im-sl14ju-part-b2.pdf, sha256 a1f9305dacbe...) gives the site-centre grid reference SU 94926 81766 (51.526838, -0.633041 with pyproj 3.7.1), a ready locator. Following the Telehouse existing-operations precedent, the operational observation takes the statement's own date, 30 June 2026 (the updated Part B3 form is dated 27 July 2026), both before the 85-day window; the 13 August publication does not renew it. LON-1 is not in the Atlas: the existing Iron Mountain record is LON-3 at 111 Buckingham Avenue, 1.16 km south-east, under separate permit EPR/TP3120LE, and its locator note says LON1/LON2 relationships created no site there. The application has no Environment Agency decision on GOV.UK or the installations register as of 22 October 2026 (GOV.UK search does not index the advertisement).
entries.reopen_condition: A dated in-window record of LON-1's operation (for example the Environment Agency's permit decision document for EPR/LP3020MX/A001, or an Iron Mountain statement naming LON-1); then add LON-1 as a new operational site at SU 94926 81766, distinct from LON-3 (different address, plot and permit).
